newsitem.title: IRAN: U.S., Britain block Gulf harmony - Rafsanjani.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Britain block Gulf harmony - Rafsanjani.

text.p: The United States and Britain are the main obstacle to better relations between Iran and its Gulf Arab neighbours, the Islamic republic's outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said over the weekend.
"I see the influence of America and Britain as the main problem in this regard," he said in a farewell interview with Jomhouri-ye Eslami daily newspaper published on Saturday.

"Close relations between Iran and Moslem neighbouring countries does not serve their interests. And they have at their disposal means to damage our relations," said Rafsanjani, who hands over to president-elect Mohammad Khatami next month.

"In talks with these Arab brothers, they (the Arabs) distinguish their interests, and realise that it is necessary for us to be friends and to cooperate. However, the colonialists do have some influence, which renders dubious the extent of the success and continuity of such relations."
Rafsanjani said a recent message from Saudi Arabia's King Fahd and Crown Prince Abdullah showed willingness to have more talks and cooperation with Iran.

But, about Iran's policy of creating a collective security treaty in the Gulf, Rafsanjani said: "The main obstacle is America and Britain. They do not let such a treaty take shape. Arab brothers themselves do not have any problem with us. If America does not hinder, the grounds are ready. But the hindrance is serious."

Relations between Tehran and Riyadh have been strained since Shi'ite Moslem clergymen led an Islamic revolution that toppled the monarchy in Iran in 1979. They severed diplomatic ties from 1988 to 1991 after the death of Iranian pilgrims in riots during the 1987 haj to the Moslem holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia.

The two states, among the world's largest oil producers, continue to differ over the presence of Western forces in the Gulf, Tehran's armaments programme, the annual pilgrimage, and charges that Iran meddles in Gulf Arab affairs -- denied by Iran.
Tehran Times newspaper, commenting on Rafsanjani's remarks, said on Sunday: "If humility is the mark of a truly great man, forgiveness is the mark of a God-fearing state.
"There is really no reason to suspect Iran's motives; it has already proved its sincerity in its relations with the Persian Gulf countries by showing the divine characteristic of forgiveness."

In this context the daily mentioned Gulf Arab funding of what it called "the Iraqi war machine" during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war and Iranian neutrality during the 1991 Gulf War over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.

"But for more than a decade our Arab brethren have been listening to the absurd propaganda the Zionists and the U.S. have cooked up against Iran, projecting Tehran as a threat to their common interests," the newspaper said.
